claims.statement: A portfolio is a user-owned named grouping of accounts, stored as `PortfolioModel` (id, user_id, name, timestamps) plus the `PortfolioAccountModel` join table whose composite primary key is `(portfolio_id, account_id)`; it stores no positions, and both FKs cascade `all, delete-orphan` from their parent relationships. The pair ships in `migrations/versions/7e1953e28527_add_portfoliomodel_and_.py` with a `UniqueConstraint('user_id', 'name')` on portfolios, and `deleted_at` exists on the model and migration but is never written because deletion is a hard ORM delete.

`PortfolioRepository` is an abstract interface in `src/account/repository.py` (`get`, `get_by_user`, `create`, `sync_accounts`, `update`, `delete`, all schema-typed) implemented by `SqlAlchemyPortfolioRepository`, whose `get`/`get_by_user` selectinload the `portfolio_accounts → account` chain and project each membership into a full `AccountSchema`, and whose `sync_accounts` is a full replacement (delete all membership rows then insert the new set, deduplicated via `set(...)`) rather than a diff. The interface/implementation pair is registered in `src/account/registry.py` via `sqlalchemy_portfolio_repository_factory`, next to `PortfolioService`.

`PortfolioService` validates before every write but does not itself compare `user_id`: `create_portfolio` and `sync_portfolio_accounts` call `AccountService.check_accounts_belong_to_user` first, `update_portfolio`/`delete_portfolio`/`sync_portfolio_accounts` call `get_portfolio` first (raising `PortfolioNotFoundError` on an unknown id instead of silently no-oping), and `check_accounts_belong_to_user` is a set-superset test over the caller's own accounts that rejects both foreign and nonexistent account ids with `AccountsDoNotBelongToUserError`.

`portfolio_router` (prefix `/portfolios`, mounted under `/api/v1`) exposes exactly five handlers — `GET /` (list for the current user), `POST /` (`{ name, accounts }` create), `PUT /{portfolio_id}/accounts` (full membership replacement), `PATCH /{portfolio_id}` (rename), `DELETE /{portfolio_id}` (hard delete returning a bare 204) — with no single-portfolio GET and no endpoint that changes name and membership together.

The three id-addressed portfolio routes each run `AuthorizationApi.check_entity_owned_by_user(user, portfolio)` in the router in addition to the service's own checks; that helper raises `HTTPException(404, "Entity does not exist")` for both a missing entity and one owned by another user, so a foreign portfolio is indistinguishable from an absent one and `test_portfolio_{update,delete,accounts_update}_not_owned` assert 404 exactly like their `*_not_found` siblings. `portfolio_accounts_sync` additionally repeats the account-ownership check at the router level before delegating, so no membership `DELETE` is issued until existence, portfolio ownership and account ownership have all passed.

Deleting a portfolio cascades through `PortfolioModel.portfolio_accounts` (`all, delete-orphan`) and removes its `portfolio_accounts` rows but never touches the accounts or their positions; symmetrically, `SqlAlchemyAccountRepository.delete` explicitly deletes the account's `PortfolioAccountModel` rows (and `PositionModel` rows) before the account row, so no dangling membership survives an account deletion.

Portfolio request validation and failure semantics: `PortfolioCreate` requires both `name` and `accounts` and `PortfolioUpdateRequest` declares `name: str = Field(..., min_length=1)`, so malformed bodies are 422; unknown portfolio ids are 404; foreign or nonexistent account ids raise `AccountsDoNotBelongToUserError` (an `AuthorizationError`, not a 404); and a duplicate `(user_id, name)` surfaces as a raw database `IntegrityError` because no uniqueness pre-check exists in `PortfolioService`.

`frontend/src/routes/portfolios/+page.server.ts` is the strict awaited SSR shape: it reads `auth_token` from cookies, awaits `getPortfolioClient(fetch).getPortfolios(token)`, and on `ApiError` either deletes the auth cookie and throws `redirect(303, '/auth/login?clear_session=true')` for a 401 or re-throws `error(status, message)`, with any other failure becoming `error(500, 'Internal Server Error')` — all four branches pinned by `page.server.test.ts`.

The `/portfolios` page performs rename and delete entirely in a local overlay (`localPortfolios` `$state` with `portfolios = $derived(localPortfolios ?? data.portfolios ?? [])`), calling `portfolioClient.updatePortfolio` / `deletePortfolio` and rewriting the overlay, with no SvelteKit `actions` and no `invalidate`; failures only `console.error` and leave the server-provided list in place. `PortfolioListItem` drives both through `EditableTitle` (title `href` `/holdings?portfolio_id={portfolio.id}`) and a `ConfirmationModal` behind an ellipsis dropdown, and `page.svelte.test.ts` asserts the `/holdings?portfolio_id=port-N` hrefs, the rename payload, the delete call plus row removal, and a cancel path that does not call the client.

Portfolio creation lives in the accounts dashboard, not on the `/portfolios` page: `AccountsListState.handleCreatePortfolioClick()` toggles selection mode and then opens `createPortfolioModal.open(selectedAccounts)` with `string[]` ids, and `create-portfolio-modal.svelte` pre-fills `Portfolio - {YYYY-MM-DD}`, client-side rejects an empty name or empty selection, then posts `portfolioClient.createPortfolio({ name: name.trim(), accounts: modalState.data })`, closing and calling `onCreated` on success while surfacing the error inside the still-open dialog on failure.

`PortfolioClient` (`frontend/src/lib/api/portfolioClient.ts`) wraps `GET /portfolios/`, `POST /portfolios/`, `PATCH /portfolios/{id}` and `DELETE /portfolios/{id}` and exposes no method for `PUT /portfolios/{id}/accounts`, so account membership can only be set at creation time through the UI even though the backend sync endpoint exists; `Portfolio.accounts` is a full `Account[]` from `frontend/src/lib/types/portfolio.ts`, which is what the holdings filter consumes.

The portfolio client module exports both `getPortfolioClient(customFetch)` — the factory SSR uses with SvelteKit's load `fetch` — and `portfolioClient`, a module-level singleton used by browser-side callers, so a test cannot intercept the singleton through a stubbed `fetch` and must mock the whole module; every portfolio UI suite does (`portfolios/page.svelte.test.ts`, `create-portfolio-modal.test.ts`), while the two server loads mock the factory, and `portfolioClient.test.ts` is the only suite exercising the real class against a `vi.fn()` `global.fetch`.

The `/holdings` filter seam resolves a portfolio client-side into account ids: `+page.server.ts` returns `portfolio_id` / `account_id` from `url.searchParams` verbatim alongside the `portfolios` and `accounts` lists fetched in the same `Promise.allSettled` pass without filtering holdings, and the page's first `$effect` looks the portfolio up in `data.portfolios`, maps `portfolio.accounts.map(a => a.id)` and calls `service.filterByPortfolio(data.portfolio_id, accountIds)`, with an unknown id degrading to an empty account list rather than an error. A dropdown selection repeats the resolution and `goto`s `/holdings?portfolio_id={id}` with `replaceState: true, noScroll: true, keepFocus: true`.

`HoldingsService.filterByPortfolio(portfolioId, accountIds)` stores the `{ type: 'portfolio', portfolioId, accountIds }` variant and the `rows` getter keeps only rows whose `account_id` is in `accountIds`, so a portfolio narrows holdings by an account-id membership test rather than a query parameter on `getUserHoldings`; the page renders the portfolio name in a breadcrumb instead of a subtitle (a subtitle exists only in the unfiltered state) and keys the "No holdings match the selected filter." empty message off that filter state.

`tests/routers/test_portfolios.py` pins the router contract end to end: empty and populated list reads, create with one and several accounts, 422 for missing `name`/`accounts` and for an empty or missing rename name, membership sync that adds, removes, keeps and empties the set (including `accounts: []`), 404 for unknown and foreign portfolios on sync, rename and delete, rename reflected in the following list, and `DELETE` returning 204 followed by disappearance from the list — backed by the `test_portfolios`, `test_portfolio_with_accounts` and `other_user_portfolio` fixtures in `tests/fixtures/account.py`.

`PortfolioListItem` takes only `portfolio`, an optional `onRename(newName)` and an optional `onDelete()`, and its action surface is three affordances: the `EditableTitle` title link to `/holdings?portfolio_id={portfolio.id}` (`showEditButton={false}`, `isEditing` bound to the component's local `isEditingTitle`), a `Rename` dropdown item that sets `isEditingTitle = true`, and a destructive `Delete portfolio` item that opens a `ConfirmationModal` whose confirm calls `onDelete?.()`. The card exposes no membership action, matching the absent `PortfolioClient` method for `PUT /portfolios/{id}/accounts`.

The card's rename path is `EditableTitle`, whose `save` handler calls `onSave` only when the edited value differs from the current value and treats Escape as a cancel, so an unmodified title issues no `updatePortfolio` request.

Each portfolio card's headline figures come from member accounts' server-computed totals rather than from holdings rows: `loadTotals` fans `accountClient.getAccountTotals` out over `portfolio.accounts` with `Promise.allSettled`, dropping any rejected account, and `aggregateAccountTotals` folds the survivors into one bucket per currency rendered by `TotalProfitLossButtons` with `testIdPrefix` `portfolio-{id}-{currency}` and never summed across currencies. The fetch is wrapped in a `browser`-guarded `$derived.by` so nothing is requested during SSR and the card shows a `Skeleton` while pending; `page.svelte.test.ts` pins that a CAD and a USD member account produce two distinct buckets.

Because `portfolio-list-item.svelte` imports the `accountClient` module singleton to load member-account totals, `frontend/src/routes/portfolios/page.svelte.test.ts` mocks both `$lib/api/portfolioClient` and `$lib/api/accountClient` and stubs `accountClient.getAccountTotals` for every test, whereas the `/holdings` suites mock the `getAccountClient` factory instead.
